title: Contents Packout & Storage Pack-Back Box Line: Boxes Brought Back and Line Amount
content:
**Calculation clause.** The boxes brought back are the boxes packed recorded on the job, except that items listed on signed disposal authorizations are not brought back, each listed item counting as one packed box: when the job's signed disposal authorizations list at least one item, the boxes brought back are the boxes packed less those listed items, never below zero. The standard pack-back box line is the boxes brought back times the tier's pack-back box rate, rounded to the cent, half up.

This Contents Packout & Storage clause prices the pack-back box line of a return on Partial Contents Packout, Full Contents Packout, High-Value Contents Packout and Commercial Contents and Records Recovery jobs. For the pack-back box line of a return, and only for that line, the amount is figured as stated here; the furniture reset line and the truck-load line of a return remain under their own rules, and any other pack-back line is still billed per box and per furniture item reset at the tier's rates, rounded to the cent, half up.

## How the amounts combine

The amounts are combined in one order: the rate per box is the tier's pack-back box rate with any percentage applied first and then every add per box added; that rate per box is multiplied by the boxes brought back; every amount figured per item is added to that product, and the total is rounded once to the cent, half up, as the line amount. Half up is applied with a tolerance of one billionth of a dollar (1e-09) added before rounding, so that a figure lying on a half cent always rounds up.

The pack-back box rate is the tier figure on the product's pack-back rates table.

## Worked figures (hypothetical; a box rate of 10.00 is used for illustration, not a tier figure)

| Boxes packed | Items on signed disposal authorizations | Boxes brought back | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| 180 | none | 180 | 1,800.00 |
| 180 | 25 | 155 | 1,550.00 |
| 20 | 30 | 0 (never below zero) | 0.00 |
